grand_strategy.reading: Algeria runs the grand strategy of a rentier state whose army is the regime and whose two standing antagonists, Morocco and France, are the two neighbours it cannot choose: one across a border closed since 1994, the other across a sea that carries its gas, its diaspora and its memory. The 1962 identity of anti-colonial sovereignty, the Sahrawi referendum and the colonisation law substitute for the votes it does not get (46.1% disputed in 2024, about 21% in 2026), so every rupture is domestic currency as much as foreign policy. The paradoxical logic shows at each step: the tap that was meant to punish (the Maghreb pipeline, Spain in 2022) was also the only income, so it ran on; each door shut (Morocco, the UAE, France's embassy premises, Mali's airspace) removes a seat at the table where Washington, Paris and Rabat then decide without Algiers. Two signals that are not rows: Algiers did not vote on Resolution 2797 and has not answered the US push for talks with Rabat, and the chief of staff's reported absence from the December 2025 council on a term-extending revision (Yabiladi, single source) is a possible seam inside the regime. The thaws of 2026 (Spain, Mali, France) are not reconciliation; they are the rentier state discovering that its leverage is bounded by its customers. Grading note: Morocco stays a rival, not an adversary, by the ontology's own test: the aim Algiers declares is Sahrawi self-determination and security, not Moroccan defeat, and the Kabylie charge is the nearest it comes to an existential accusation.

stances.note: Argued from Algiers' side. Algeria cut diplomatic relations on 24 Aug 2021 over Morocco's 'hostile actions' (it blamed the August 2021 wildfires on the MAK, which it labels terrorist, and accused Rabat of backing it), the border has been shut since 1994, the Maghreb-Europe gas contract was left to lapse on 31 Oct 2021, Tebboune said in Mar 2023 that ties had passed 'the point of no return', the airspace was closed to Moroccan aircraft on 22 Sep 2021 and visas were imposed on Moroccans on 26 Sep 2024, and in Nov 2025 Attaf said bilateral dialogue with Morocco 'is not on the agenda' while Washington mediates; S/RES/2797 names Algeria among the parties it asks to negotiate. The Kabylie charge is the nearest Algiers comes to an existential accusation. But the ontology's test for adversary is a declared aim of the other's defeat or disappearance: Algiers declares Sahrawi self-determination, border security and the military balance, not Moroccan partition or regime change; the king has repeatedly offered to talk; Carnegie and Crisis Group speak of a rivalry (Carnegie: extending into the Sahel) and SIPRI of a long-running tension that drives arms imports, not of a war aim. Rival, stable (frozen); the grade would move to adversary only if Algiers stated an aim against Moroccan integrity or Rabat's MAK backing were proved and acted on. Bond - grievance: Western Sahara, the Sand War legacy and mutual accusation.
